# Cornelia Bryant

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v4 c8 P19](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0019), [v5 c1 P0](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0000)</sub>
- **Status:** Alive  <sub>[v5 c1 P0](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0000)</sub>
- **Titles:** Miss  <sub>[v4 c6 P37](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0037)</sub>; Mrs. Marshall Elliott  <sub>[v5 c1 P0](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0000)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** The fair Cornelia  <sub>[v5 c23 P40](../source/v05-c23.md#nw-v05-c23-p0040)</sub>

## Appearance

She has a fresh, round, pink-and-white face with jolly, kindly brown eyes. Her hard little knob of fair hair is held on her head by a tight elastic band under her capacious sun-hat, without hat pins. In later years, she maintains a comfortable, matronly figure.

_Sources: [v4 c8 P19](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0019), [v4 c11 P17](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0017), [v5 c1 P0](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0000)_

## Personality

She is sharp-tongued, blunt, and highly opinionated, outspokenly expressing her contempt for men and Methodists. Despite her grim determination and sarcastic humor, she possesses a generous, sympathetic heart, dedicated to helping neighbors and destitute children. She is an energetic, practical woman who prides herself on her independence and superior sewing abilities.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P37](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0037), [v4 c6 P38](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0038), [v4 c8 P19](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0019), [v4 c8 P26](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0026), [v4 c8 P27](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0027), [v4 c8 P47](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0047), [v4 c8 P59](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0059), [v4 c15 P10](../source/v04-c15.md#nw-v04-c15-p0010), [v5 c8 P5](../source/v05-c08.md#nw-v05-c08-p0005), [v5 c9 P25](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0025), [v5 c9 P44](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0044)_

## History

Living at Four Winds Harbor in a brilliant emerald house, Cornelia Bryant quickly introduced herself to Anne and Gilbert Blythe upon their arrival. She formed a close friendship with Anne, frequently visiting her home, sewing garments for impoverished children, and offering outspoken commentary on community events. She strongly supported Leslie Moore through her severe hardships and initially opposed Gilbert's decision to treat Dick Moore. Later, after the truth about Dick was revealed and Marshall Elliott cut his beard, she agreed to marry Marshall, whom she had known for over twenty years. Thirteen years after her marriage, she remained a central figure in Glen St. Mary, taking in and adopting the destitute orphan Mary Vance. She actively managed church matters at the local Presbyterian manse and continued visiting and helping her friends at Ingleside.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P35](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0035), [v4 c6 P37](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0037), [v4 c8 P19](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0019), [v4 c8 P25](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0025), [v4 c10 P37](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0037), [v4 c11 P11](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0011), [v4 c30 P32](../source/v04-c30.md#nw-v04-c30-p0032), [v4 c32 P0](../source/v04-c32.md#nw-v04-c32-p0000), [v4 c37 P0](../source/v04-c37.md#nw-v04-c37-p0000), [v4 c37 P9](../source/v04-c37.md#nw-v04-c37-p0009), [v4 c37 P10](../source/v04-c37.md#nw-v04-c37-p0010), [v5 c1 P0](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0000), [v5 c1 P1](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0001), [v5 c9 P42](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0042), [v5 c9 P44](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0044)_

## Background by volume

- Was an only child for eight years before her brother was born  <sub>[v4 c34 P26](../source/v04-c34.md#nw-v04-c34-p0026)</sub>
- Her only brother died fifteen years prior to her meeting an evangelist  <sub>[v4 c28 P7](../source/v04-c28.md#nw-v04-c28-p0007)</sub>
- Won first prize for lemon pies at the Charlottetown Exhibition  <sub>[v4 c10 P35](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0035)</sub>

## Quotes

> I’m the best sewer in these parts. I ought to be! Lord, I’ve done more of it than if I’d had a hundred children of my own, believe ME!  <sub>[v4 c8 P27](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0027)</sub>

> Lord, dearie, I don’t hate them. They aren’t worth it. I just sort of despise them.  <sub>[v4 c8 P59](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0059)</sub>

> I’m not hankering after the vote, believe ME. I know what it is to clean up after the men.  <sub>[v4 c15 P37](../source/v04-c15.md#nw-v04-c15-p0037)</sub>

> I shall never have truck or trade with Methodists, and Mr. Meredith will find that he’d better steer clear of them, too.  <sub>[v5 c2 P43](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0043)</sub>

> I’ve got a shorter catechism and a small tooth comb and I’m going to do my duty by her, now that I’ve set my hand to the plough, believe me.  <sub>[v5 c9 P44](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0044)</sub>
